taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripe in August and September, after the July and August flowers.

generator.params.note: Evergreen huckleberry's (vaccinium-ovatum) values, changed by hand for pink mountain-heather: a low, dense mat of many erect branches from near the ground (Abrams 1951 p. 303: "Low much-branched matted shrub with erect branches, 1-5 dm. high"), short internodes, sprigs of crowded needle-like leaves kept for several years, and a small cluster of nodding flowers at each shoot's tip. Not fitted to measurements.

appearance.organs.bloom.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 303, Phyllodoce empetriformis: "flowers few to many; pedicels 12-25 mm. long"; "corolla campanulate, rose-pink, not constricted at the throat, 5-8 mm. long"; "capsule globose". Drawn as an umbel of 6 nodding rose-pink bells on long stalks, each about twice the brown capsule's size.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a dense, low mat of erect stems clothed in short, dark green, needle-like leaves, each stem topped by a cluster of nodding rose-pink bells on long red stalks. Organ cards from evergreen huckleberry's (vaccinium-ovatum), recoloured and resized by hand. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

allometry.note: 0.25 m tall at 10 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows in subalpine parkland. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

traits.stem_clump.note: Flora of North America vol. 8 p. 476 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Phyllodoce empetriformis: "Plants prostrate to erect, diffusely branched, 0.5-5 dm"; Abrams (1951 p. 303): "Low much-branched matted shrub with erect branches".
